clue.text: Villain’s wife mostly felt bad, turning up to embrace me

indicators.note: most but not all of something means its final letter is dropped
in a down entry, turning something upwards makes it read from bottom to top
to embrace is to hug, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: to ail is to be unwell, so felt bad is ailed
the sol-fa note mi is also spelt 'me'

explanation.surface: A wicked man's wife, unhappy, hugs the speaker as she gets up.
explanation.walkthrough: The villain is Iago from Shakespeare's Othello. 'Me' is an accepted spelling of the sol-fa note usually written mi.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's Othello the scheming Iago is married to Emilia, who finally exposes his plot.

clue.text: Everyone concentrated without power being assigned

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the named letter is taken away

blocks.note: everyone is all
potted means condensed or abridged, as in a potted history
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: A group all focused hard, without any energy left, while receiving tasks.
explanation.walkthrough: Concentrated here means condensed, as in a potted history, not mentally focused. P is the physics symbol for power.
explanation.definitionFit: Something allotted has been given out as a share, so it is the state of having been handed out to someone.

clue.text: Interference not shifting?

blocks.note: first meaning: crackle that spoils a radio or TV signal
second meaning: motionless, staying in one place

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark invites reading the two parts as one idea about stubborn meddling; they are two separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Atmospheric crackle on a broadcast is called this noun, and the same word as an adjective describes anything stationary.

clue.text: Ladies drink

blocks.note: first meaning: a group, traditionally of women
second meaning: informal British word (also spelt bevvy) for an alcoholic drink

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a sign for a women's bar. A bevy is a collective noun for women or quails, and bevvy or bevy is British slang for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The collective noun traditionally used for a group of women, and also a British slang term for booze.

clue.text: Exaggerated fictions seeing one abandoned in parts of churches

indicators.note: something abandoned is left behind, so the named letter goes missing

blocks.note: steep means excessive or unreasonable, as in a steep price
fictions are untruths
Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Tall stories mean one person has been left behind somewhere inside church buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: Steep for exaggerated is the informal sense of an over-the-top claim or price; one is the Roman numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeple is the tall tower with a spire rising from a church, so these are sections of such buildings.

clue.text: Old confusion about limitations of toast and egg dish

indicators.note: limitations are boundaries, so only the edge letters of the word are kept
about means surrounding, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
a melee is a confused scramble or brawl
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A muddled breakfast order involving toast and an egg dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limitations of toast' sounds like a complaint about bread, but it means only the word's two edges are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaten eggs fried in a pan and folded over a filling make this classic French-named preparation.

clue.text: Wake up, making love with a heavenly body?

blocks.note: a comet is a body that travels through space
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A romantic encounter with a gorgeous partner is enough to stir someone from sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly body' looks like flattery for an attractive person, but it is literal: a comet in the sky. Love is O from tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover consciousness after fainting or sleep is a common phrasal verb meaning to regain awareness.

clue.text: Charles and Anne, perhaps, in structural framework

blocks.note: Chas is the standard short form of Charles
Anne is an example of a sister, informally sis

explanation.surface: Royal siblings Charles and Anne at the heart of the institution's structure.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles and Anne are the royal brother and sister, which is why Anne can be a 'sis'; 'perhaps' marks her as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The chassis is the base frame of a car or other machine, onto which the body and parts are fixed.

clue.text: Neat French phrase provided the theme

blocks.note: a mot is a witty saying, from French bon mot
if means provided that

explanation.surface: A tidy French expression set the tone for the whole piece.
explanation.walkthrough: A mot (as in bon mot) is a clever remark, borrowed from French, so 'neat French phrase' points to it as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A recurring idea or pattern running through a work of art or music is its dominant motif.

clue.text: A large aggressive man, completely exhausted

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large
a lout is a rough, violent man

explanation.surface: A big brute of a man who has worn himself out entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: The clothing-size L for large joins A and LOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Going all out means using every ounce of effort, so the phrase can describe being spent and drained.

clue.text: Increasingly barmy positive votes preceding row

blocks.note: yeas are votes in favour
a tier is a row or level, as of seats

explanation.surface: A parliamentary row grows ever more crazy as the ayes pile up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barmy' looks like slang for mad, but barm is the froth on fermenting beer, so barmy literally means frothy with yeast.
explanation.definitionFit: Barm is yeast froth, so the comparative of barmy is the comparative of full of ferment.

clue.text: Religious interventions if curate’s active around husband

indicators.note: active means busy and moving, so the letters are set in motion into a new order
around means on every side, so one piece is placed inside another

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged, taking the apostrophe s as S
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A vicar busying himself about a married man, trying to heal him through prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in curate's is ignored, so its S counts as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Healing attributed to belief and prayer rather than medicine is a spiritual form of treatment, hence a religious intervention.

clue.text: Monarch’s hopeful, sending son out with a student

indicators.note: sending something out dispatches it away, so that letter leaves

blocks.note: rosy means optimistic, as in a rosy outlook
S is the abbreviation for son
taken as written
L for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A king's optimism as he packs his boy off with a learner companion.
explanation.walkthrough: ROSY loses its S to give ROY. The student is L, the learner plate on a British car.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for belonging to a king or queen, so a possessive like this works as a synonym.

clue.text: Perfect US fighter and ship heading off

indicators.note: with its head taken away, a word loses its first letter

blocks.note: American fighter jets are designated F, as in F-16
the hull is the body of a ship, standing for the whole

explanation.surface: An ideal American warplane and a vessel setting off together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' reads as a ship departing, but it removes the first letter of HULL. US military fighter aircraft carry the F prefix.
explanation.definitionFit: Full can mean complete or entire, with nothing missing, as in a full set, which is close to flawless.

clue.text: European currency was a thing for Rome

blocks.note: first meaning: British slang for a pound sterling
second meaning: the Latin word for something or what

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the old Roman money; instead a quid is slang for one British pound, and quid is also Latin for 'what' or 'something'.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang names the pound coin this way, and ancient Latin speakers used the same word for 'anything'.

clue.text: No main changes in Open University, reflecting speaking with one voice

indicators.note: changes means alters, so these letters take on a new arrangement
a reflection shows things back to front, so the letters run the other way
in means placed inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
OU is the abbreviation for the Open University, the UK distance-learning university

explanation.surface: A university debate where the key motion keeps being altered, while everyone reflects on agreeing.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a Latin phrase, so the fodder letters cannot be checked against an English word until the whole is assembled.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase means 'with one mind', describing unanimous agreement among a group.

clue.text: Deep times penetrating idiot

indicators.note: to penetrate is to go inside, so one piece enters another

blocks.note: by means multiplied by, as in three by four
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Profound moments getting through to a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deep' looks like an adjective, but as a noun the deep is the sea or a bottomless gulf.
explanation.definitionFit: The deep, as a noun, is a vast chasm or ocean depth, which is what this word names.

clue.text: Area, dry, containing trees initially

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for area
TT means teetotal, never drinking alcohol
firs are conifers

explanation.surface: A parched region that once had trees on it at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' usually signals first letters, but here it is the definition. Dry means teetotal, abbreviated TT.
explanation.definitionFit: Both expressions mean at the beginning or to start with, so they are interchangeable adverbs.

clue.text: Unusual attachment seeing rejection of alien sea creature

indicators.note: rejecting something throws it out, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: a fetish is an abnormal fixation
ET is the film alien, the extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: A strange fondness that leads someone to spurn an extraterrestrial marine animal.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ET out of FETISH and four letters remain.
explanation.definitionFit: A cod, trout or other gilled swimming animal living in water is the most general kind of marine life.

clue.text: Sneaky thief to head for room, getting ruby?

indicators.note: sneaky means sly and devious, so these letters are moved around craftily
the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written for the rearrangement
taken as written
the first letter of room

explanation.surface: A furtive burglar heads for a room hoping to steal a gem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruby' looks like the jewel the thief is after, but a ruby wedding is the fortieth anniversary.
explanation.definitionFit: Anniversaries are named after materials, and the ruby one marks forty years of marriage.

clue.text: Judge young men going topless to be sources of delight

indicators.note: with its top removed, a word loses its first letter

blocks.note: J is the abbreviation for judge
boys are young males

explanation.surface: A magistrate rules on lads stripping off for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' suggests bare chests, but it removes the first letter of BOYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Joys are things that bring great happiness, so they are causes of pleasure.

clue.text: Car brand adequate in promotional materials after review

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece sits within another
to review is to look back over, so the whole is read backwards

blocks.note: ads are advertisements
OK means acceptable

explanation.surface: A car maker's adverts are deemed passable once critics have looked them over.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal applies to everything after the insertion, not just to the adverts.
explanation.definitionFit: Skoda is a Czech automobile manufacturer, now part of the Volkswagen group, so it is a make of vehicle.

clue.text: Back to square one?

blocks.note: surface reading: returning to the starting point after getting nowhere
setter's reading: the italic square hints at its geometric opposite, a round shape that ends where it began

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for starting again is the obvious reading; the italics on 'square' nudge you toward a shape, and the answer is a round one.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming this way round means ending up where you started, which is exactly what the familiar idiom about square one describes.

clue.text: Going over long account will make you sleep

indicators.note: to go over is to flip, so the letters are turned to run the other way

blocks.note: to long for is to pant for, yearn
AC is the abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: Sitting through a lengthy report is enough to put anyone to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going over a long account' sounds like reviewing a tedious story; in fact PANT and AC are joined and the pair flipped.
explanation.definitionFit: A catnap is a brief doze, so as a noun it is a short period of slumber.

clue.text: Story about modern innovation’s to form link

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: a story can be a falsehood, a fib
AI, artificial intelligence, is a recent innovation; plus the S of the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A tale about a new invention is meant to bring people together.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s is kept as a letter. AI, artificial intelligence, is the modern innovation.
explanation.definitionFit: To liaise is to act as a go-between or cooperate, setting up communication between parties.

clue.text: European native with mostly limited backing

indicators.note: most but not all of something means its final letter is dropped
backing means moving backwards, so the letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: and means along with
narrow means restricted

explanation.surface: A citizen of Europe whose support is largely restricted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like support, but it signals the letters running in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone born in the tiny Pyrenean principality between France and Spain is a citizen of that country.

clue.text: Scruffy area, apparently in North-East

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: app. or ap. is a dictionary abbreviation for apparently
NE is the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: A run-down district, it seems, in the north-east of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scruffy area' suggests a shabby neighbourhood, but it is the area of the scruff, the back of the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: The scruff is the back of the neck, so the zone where an animal is held by its scruff is this body part.

clue.text: Court case about book describing clans?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: a trial is a hearing in court
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A lawsuit over a book written about family clans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describing clans' is the definition, since an adjective describes; B goes inside TRIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to tribes, groups bound by kinship, which is what clans are.

clue.text: Superior couple of points penned by actual musician, with a twist

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, as in a pen, so the letters lie inside the words
a twist turns something round, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A top pair of performers signed up by a real musician, with an unexpected turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Superior' is used in the printing sense of placed above, as in superscript.
explanation.definitionFit: An umlaut is the pair of dots written above a vowel in German, so a superscript pair of marks.

clue.text: Pay hasn’t changed? Unrealistic expectation

indicators.note: changed means altered, so these letters take on a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Hoping for a pay rise when wages are frozen is just wishful thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: PHANTASY is an older spelling of fantasy, still used in literary and psychoanalytic writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A fantasy is an imagined hope with little basis in reality, so a daydream that will not come true.
